EVA.Blobs.Services.CreateBlob.description:
Creates a new, empty blob. If you wish to store data in there directly, use the `StoreBlob` service instead.

Empty blobs are placeholders; eventually, you'll want to push data in there. This service allows you to create that placeholder, and it is expected you then use the
multipart or raw binary `POST` call to `/blob/{Guid}` to push your data.

The combination of `Category` and `OriginalName` must be unique, as the `GetBlobInfoService` allows retrieval based on these values. Internally, a fresh and unique `Guid` is
generated and returned from this request. The response also contains the full `Url` by which this blob can be accessed (which will contain aforementioned `Guid`). Use this
path to POST your data, too!

- [x] The `MimeType` is required, a few suggestions would be `application/pdf`, `text/csv` or `application/json` - but you probably already know this.
- [x] The `ExpireDate` is the date at which the given blob should expire. Leave this empty to *suggest* to keep it forever. We will bag it and get rid of it when the time is right. :hocho:

When retrieving the blob, it will be returned to you using the `MimeType` as `ContentType` header and a proper `Expires` header.

Guid.description: The ID of the newly created blob.

Url.description: The URL where the newly created blob can be accessed.

BlobID.description: Can be used for standard blobs - for secure blobs, use `BlobUrl` instead.

EVA.Blobs.Services.StoreBlob.description:
Creates a new blob and stores `Data` to it.

The combination of `Category` and `OriginalName` must be unique, as the `GetBlobInfoService` allows retrieval based on these values. Internally, a fresh and unique `Guid` is
generated and returned from this request. The response also contains the full `Url` by which this blob can be accessed (which will contain aforementioned `Guid`).

- [x] The `MimeType` is required, a few suggestions would be `application/pdf`, `text/csv` or `application/json` - but you probably already know this.
- [x] The `ExpireDate` is the date at which the given blob should expire. Leave this empty to *suggest* to keep it forever. We will bag it and get rid of it when the time is right. :hocho:

When retrieving the blob, it will be returned to you using the `MimeType` as `ContentType` header and a proper `Expires` header.

*NOTE*: leaving `OriginalName` empty means EVA treats this file as a temporary one and it'll be removed after a set period. Which can be manipulated through the setting `Blobs:DefaultLifeTime`
which is the default expire time for these kinds of blobs in minutes.

EVA.Core.Auditing.ListEventLedger.description:
This service lets you query the EventLedger for auditing purposes.

The request provides a PageConfig (of type ScrollablePageConfig) that lets you filter on the given properties in the EventLedger.
Paging is done by providing the request with the `NextResultToken` that you got back from the previous request.
As this method of paging is forward-only, you can't go back to a previous page unless you store the token or the results,
and the total number of results is unknown, only whether or not there are more results (determined by if the NextResultToken is null).

The response contains the whole EventLedger document.

Possible filters:

- Types: A list of strings that refer to the `Type` field that is in every document.
- OrderID: Only return documents that contain a reference to the given OrderID
- OrganizationUnitID: Only return documents that were created by someone logged into the given OrganizationUnitID. It's recommended that this filter is always used, due to performance reasons.
- DeviceID: Filters on documents that have a reference to the given device, usually associated with a payment or a print command.
- FromDate: Only return documents newer than this date. It's recommended that this filter is always used, due to performance reasons.
- ToDate: Only return documents older than this date. It's recommended that this filter is always used, due to performance reasons.
- UserIDs: Only return documents created by these users. The IDs for this can be gotten by first doing a user search.
- FirstName: Filter on documents created by users whose first name starts with this. Achieves the same as filtering on UserIDs, but with one step less. However, due to privacy reasons, this information isn't stored for customers.
- FullName: Filter on documents created by users whose full name starts with this. Achieves the same as filtering on UserIDs, but with one step less. However, due to privacy reasons, this information isn't stored for customers.
- EmailAddress: Filter on documents created by users whose email starts with this. Achieves the same as filtering on UserIDs, but with one step less. However, due to privacy reasons, this information isn't stored for customers.

EVA.Core.Authentication.CreatePasskey.description:
After having called `GetPasskeyChallenge` to obtain a challenge and some information from the server, and after pushing that through WebAuthn using `navigator.credentials.create`,
you extract information from the generated credential and send it back to the server for storage.

1. The `Challenge` matching the one originally provided through `GetPasskeyChallenge`
2. The `PublicKey` generated (base64 encoded)
3. The `AuthenticatorData` generated (base64 encoded)

The creation will succeed if the `Challenge` matches the one we created for you and all the data checks out, after which you can use your new key to log in!

When you want to log in, simply call `Login` using `CustomAuthenticatorType` set to "Passkey" and it will reply with a challenge and some information inside the
`CustomAuthenticateResponseData` property, which you can push through WebAuthn using `navigator.credentials.get` to sign that challenge with your private key. Exact the information
from the generated credential and call `Login` again with the same `CustomAuthenticatorType`, but this time include `CustomAuthenticateData` with an object of type
`PasskeyAuthenticateMessage` containing;

- The `ID` as the "rawId" of the used credential (base64 encoded)
- The `Signature` that was created to sign the challenge (base64 encoded)
- The `ClientData` to include some client information (base64 encoded json)
- The `AuthenticatorData` to include some authenticator data (base64 encoded)

If this all checks out, you're logged in! As with every `Login`, be sure to specify user types and organization units of your preference.

EVA.Core.Authentication.GenerateElevatio.description:
Generates an elevation barcode to elevate this user's rights, which can be scanned by a manager with sufficient rights to grant elevation.

Show the returned `Barcode` to a manager for scanning through the `ParseBarcode` service, preferably as QR code through our `/barcode` endpoint.

:shield: Requires `Security:ElevatedFunctionalityProvider` to contain "ElevationBarcode".

:point_right: Send the returned `RequestToken` as elevation header with your original call, but before you do, it needs to be confirmed first through a manager scan. You can use this
same token to subscribe to the `/elevationBarcode` SignalR hub to listen for this scan event.

:bulb: Supply the `OrganizationUnitID` of your current context, and the `Functionality`, `Scope` and `ElevationType` returned from your original request through response headers
`EVA-Elevation-Functionality`, `EVA-Elevation-Scope` and `EVA-Elevation-Type` respectively.

Generates an elevation skip token to elevate this user's rights.

:shield: Requires `Security:ElevatedFunctionalityProvider` to contain "Skip".

:point_right: Simply use this as elevation header with your original call, you don't need anyone else for this elevation.

:bulb: Supply the `OrganizationUnitID` of your current context, and the `Functionality`, `Scope` and `ElevationType` returned from your original request through response headers
`EVA-Elevation-Functionality`, `EVA-Elevation-Scope` and `EVA-Elevation-Type` respectively.

ElevationSkipReasonID.description: Required when `Security:RequireElevationSkipReason` is enabled. Use `GetElevationSkipReasons` to get the available reasons.

EVA.Core.Authentication.GenerateTemporar.description:
Generates a temporary 5-digit code that can be used for elevation.

A manager generates this code on their own device, and can then manually copy this code on the user's device when requested.

:shield: Requires `Security:ElevatedFunctionalityProvider` to contain "TemporaryElevationCode".

:point_right: Send this temporary code as elevation header with your original call.

:bulb: Note it's only valid for a limited period of time (as per `Security:TemporaryElevationCode:ExpireInMinutes`) and is a /separate/ code from your login PIN!

EVA.Core.Cart.GetShoppingCart.description:
This returns the requested order. The order is retreived based on the OrderID.

The order will be recalculated:
- Discounts
- ShippingCosts
- GiftWrappingCosts
- OrderLine prices

If no recalculation is needed, use the GetOrder service instead. In general the approach would be: use GetShoppingCart while building the order, after PrepareOrderForCheckout has been called, switch to GetOrder.

To include the result of `GetRequiredDataForOrder`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.RequiredFor` can be set to the desired level of requirements.
To include the result of `GetProductRequirementValuesForOrder`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludeProductRequirements` can be set to `true`.
To include the result of `GetGiftWrappingOptionsForOrder` and `GetAvailableGiftWrappingLinesForOrder`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludeGiftWrapping` can be set to `true`.
To include the result of `PrefigureDiscounts` and `GetPotentialDiscountsForOrder`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludePrefigureDiscounts` can be set to `true`.
To include the result of `GetPickProductDiscountOptionsForOrder`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludePickProductOptions` can be set to `true`.
To include the result of `ListAvailableShippingMethods`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludeAvailableShippingMethods` can be set to `true`.
To include the result of `GetAvailablePaymentMethods`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludeAvailablePaymentMethods` can be set to `true`.
To include the result of `GetAvailableRefundPaymentMethodsForOrder`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludeAvailableRefundPaymentMethods` can be set to `true`.
To include the result of `ValidateOrderShipment`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludeValidateShipment` can be set to `true`.
To include the available actions for the PaymentTransactions, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludePaymentTransactionActions` can be set to `true`.

EVA.Core.Discounts.PrefigureDiscounts.description:
List the discounts that potentially could be activated.

A order or user can be given to look at the context of the order or user. When order is given the user will be ignored and the customer of the order will be used (if present)

If a `ProductIDs`, `ProductSearchID` or `ProductSearch` is set, the service will check if the resulting products are a eligible to one or more discounts. If an `OrderID` is provided, the context of the given order is taken into account, that can include user specific discounts, order OU specific discount, etc.

Be aware that:
- If `ProductIDs` is given, `ProductSearchID` and `ProductSearch` are ignored
- If `ProductSearchID` is given, `ProductIDs` and `ProductSearch` are ignored
- If `ProductSearch` is given, `ProductIDs` and `ProductSearchID` are ignored

DeactivationReasons.description:
You can filter discounts based on their deactivation reason.The array is interpreted as an 'or' value list
To get discounts with a specific deactivation reason, only provide the deactivation reason you want. For example:
- providing an empty value will return all discounts
- providing `None` (0) will return discounts that are active.
- providing `Unverified` (1) will return discounts that are inactive because they are unverified.
- providing `Unverified` (1) and `DisabledByUser` (2) will return discounts that are inactive because they are either unverified OR disabled by user.
- providing `Unverified` (1) and `DisabledByUser` (2) as a combined flag (3) will return discounts that are inactive because they are unverified AND disabled by user.

EVA.Core.Enums.GetEnumValues.description:
A generic service to return all possible values in specified list, e.g. `Currency`, `TaxCode` or `StockLabel`.

The `Name` of the enumeration is unique within EVA, and all of the `Values` returned are also unique and identifiable
by their respective `Name`. Services that consume a value of an enumeration will expect the numeric `Value` returned.

Some of these enumerations are static and are defined by code, meaning the `Values`' combination of `Name` and `Value`
is contant and will never change. It is important to know, though, that other enumerations may be dynamic and can be
altered per environment by their own respective services. When using these, keep in mind they can vary between
environments and new values could be added. It is guaranteed, however, that once a certain `Name`-`Value` pair is set,
it will never change in that particular environment and you are safe treat it as a constant.

:point_right: It is important to realize these dynamics, because at first sight, all of these values may seem contant between
environments - but that is the mere result of an initialization sequence that is usually identical, but definitely
not guaranteed!

:point_right: `IsFlags` will indicate if the values should be treated as bit fields (or, a set of flags). For example,
the enumeration `OrganizationUnitTypes` demonstrates that an organization unit can both be a Shop (`1`) and a Warehouse (`16`)
at the same time, indicated by value `17`. Always use bitwise operands on these fields!

EVA.Core.EventExportConfigurations.Creat.description:
Create event export configurations.

Event Export Configurations allow you to configure specific endpoints (webhooks) for EventTargets and EventTypes.

- Not setting EventTarget & EventType will configure the endpoint for all targets and types

BackendID.description: An optional identifier used by external systems to reference this configuration.

ConcurrentRequests.description: The maximum number of concurrent outgoing calls we make.

EndpointConfigurationID.description: The configuration of the endpoint attached to this EventExport.

Name.description: A name to identify the configuration.

Certificate.description: A client certificate that can be used for mTLS. Must be X509 in PKCS12 format. Also, it must not be expired, have a private key and have clientAuth in it's extended key usage.

Password.description: The password that is used to encrypt the certificate.

StaticBearerToken.description: This will result in an authorization header that looks like: `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN`

StaticUnschemedToken.description: This will result in an authorization header that looks like: `Authorization: TOKEN`. Use this only when the other options are not sufficient.

Authorization.description: Authorization configuration used when calling this endpoint.

ExcludedMessageTypes.description: Exclude certain message types. If not set, no message types will be excluded.

ExcludeOrganizationUnits.description: Exclude certain organization units. If not set, no organization units will be excluded.

ExcludeOrganizationUnitSets.description: Exclude certain organization unit sets. If not set, no organization units will be excluded.

IncludeOrganizationUnits.description: Filter for certain organization units. If not set, all organization units will be sent.

IncludeOrganizationUnitSets.description: Filter for certain organization unit sets. If not set, all organization units will be sent.

MessageTypes.description: Filter for certain message types. If not set, all message types will be sent.

Protocol.description: The protocol to use when sending the data. If not set, the best available version of HTTP will be used.

ResponseMode.description: Defines what kind of response EVA requires from this endpoint.

ScriptID.description: Optional script to run before sending the data. This can be used to filter out the event export.

ScriptName.description: Name of the script that ScriptID refers to.

TimeoutSeconds.description: Timeout after which event exports are cancelled. Defaults to 5 seconds. Not recommended to change.

ConcurrentRequests.description: The maximum number of concurrent outgoing calls we make.

EffectiveStatus.description: The effective status of this configuration. Reflects the endpoint's status when the endpoint is disabled or in error.

EndpointConfigurationID.description: ID of the linked EndpointConfiguration. Null if the endpoint has been deleted.

EndpointStatus.description: Status of the linked EndpointConfiguration. Null if the endpoint has been deleted.

Status.description: The status of this configuration itself, independent of the endpoint's status.

EVA.Core.Finance.CompleteCloseCashJourna.description:
Completes the closing of a cash journal, making the device once again unavailable for cash transactions until a new journal is opened.

This service expects a list of coins and notes, which summed up must equal the given `TotalAmount`.

If the `TotalAmount` is different from what was expected (returned as `ExpectedClosingAmount` in `StartCloseCashJournal` ) then this deviation
must be corrected and provided through a list of corrections in the `Corrections` field.

For cash journals that either do not use or ignore cash journals, most properties will automatically be set to the expected amounts. Should you
want to enforce validation, regardless, specify the `ForceValidation` as `true`.

Pending cash deposits need to be accounted for as well - supply their `ID`s as `PendingCashDeposits`. Do not add the `Amount` of cash deposits
to the `TotalAmount`, as the user cannot usually verify the cash deposit content.

EVA.Core.Finance.CompleteOpenCashJournal.description:
Completes the opening of a cash journal. After this service has been called, it's possible to make cash transactions on this device.

This service expects a list of the coins and notes that were counted.

When the opening amount is different from last period's closing amount, it's required that a correction is provided for this difference
in `OpeningDeviationCorrection`. This simply consists of a description and an amount.

For cash journals that either do not use or ignore cash journals, most properties will automatically be set to the expected amounts. Should you
want to enforce validation, regardless, specify the `ForceValidation` as `true`.

Pending cash deposits need to be accounted for as well - supply their `ID`s as `PendingCashDeposits`. Do not add the `Amount` of cash deposits
to the `TotalAmount`, as the user cannot usually verify the cash deposit content.

EVA.Core.Finance.CreateCashDeposit.description:

When not explicitly delaying the drop-off, it will be booked to the current active cash journal and financial period.

EVA.Core.Finance.CreateCashExpense.description:
Creates a cash expense.

This service expects:
- `DeviceID`, which is the cash device the money was used from.
- `TypeID` which is one of the available expense types.
- An `Amount`, which is the amount of cash that was taken from or added to the device.
The amount should always be positive, but the semantics of the amount depends on the AmountType of the ExpenseType:
if ExpenseType.AmountType = Expense, then the amount is booked as an expense, if it's Income then it's booked as income. Either way, it should be a positive number.
- A `TaxCodeID`, which refers to one of the available tax codes.
- A `Description`, which is the reason for this expense (for example: 'lunch').
- A `BlobID`, which contains an image of the receipt.
- A `SignatureBlobID`, which contains an image of the signature

BlobID.description: Optional image of the receipt

EVA.Core.Finance.GetFinancialPeriodClosi.description:
Gets a list of reasons (if any) why this period cannot be closed yet.

The current possible reasons are (which is available in the `Type` property of each item):

## CLOCKED_IN_USER

The user is still clocked in and must be clocked out.

### Data

The `Data` property will contain:

```json
{
  "UserID" : 1,
  "ClockedIn" : "2018-08-01 12:00",
  "FirstName" : "John",
  "LastName"  : "Doe"
}
```

## ACTIVE_USER_TASK

The user task hasn't been completed yet and it's either attached to this financial period, or its past its deadline.

### Data

The `Data` property will contain:

```json
{
	"UserTaskID" : 5546,
	"UserTaskTypeID" : 9,
	"UserID" : null,
	"UserFullName" : null,
	"IsActive" : true,
	"IsCompleted" : false,
	"Deadline" : null,
	"CreationTime" : "2018-08-01"
}
```

## OPEN_CASH_JOURNAL

There is still an open cash journal that needs to be closed before the period can be closed.

### Data

The `Data` property will contain:

```json
{
"CashJournalID" : 3,
"DeviceID" : 1,
"OpeningAmount" : 150.15
}
```

## PCI_QUESTION

The PCI compliancy question has not been answered yet, this is required to close the period if the OrganizationUnit has been configured to require it.

### Data

No Data.

## NEGATIVE_STOCK

There is negative stock that must be corrected (to at least zero) before the period can be closed.

### Data

The `Data` property will contain:

```json
{
  "ProductID" : 7684,
  "ProductBackendID" : "ABC123",
  "QuantityOnHand" : -10,
  "StockLabelID" : 1,
  "StockLabelName" : "Sellable",
  "OrganizationUnitID" : 182
}
```

This data can then be used to correct the stock through AdjustStock/MoveStock.
Gets information regarding financial period stock

This organization unit should get an updated location before starting this financial period.

### Data

No Data.

which means all associated financial ledgers are deleted.

is sent to the caller of this service with the results.

The scope of which events to reset can be limited by specifying a `Filter` in the request. Only the events
that match the filter will be reset.

EVA.Core.Finance.StartCloseCashJournal.description:
Initiates the closing of a cash journal. This does not yet mutate anything, but returns all the details you need about a cash journal to be able to close it.

This consists of:

- The information about the device and station
- Which expenses and deposits were made from this device.
- What payments were made.
- What the `ExpectedClosingAmount` is, which is a summary of the previous journal's closing amount plus all transactions.
- Possible pending cash deposits on this device

EVA.Core.Finance.StartOpenCashJournal.description:
Starts the opening of a cash journal for the given DeviceID.

It's only possible to open a cash journal when an open financial period exists and when the device is a cash device. Retrieving a list of valid devices
can be accomplished through the `ListDevices` service.

Calling this service does not yet do anything, except return the data you need to open a cash journal:

- The available denominations (coins and notes)
- The details about the previous cash journal's closing amounts (if it exists), which can be used as an extra check
- Possible pending cash deposits on this device

      When this property is false, the result will be processed as a full set. Matching values will be updated, new values will be added and existing values no present in the CountResults will be removed.

For each combination of FullStockCountLabelName and StockLabelName, an FSC-label is created when it does not exist yet.
Labels created this way are marked as externally created and remain open, so they can be inspected and corrected in the tasks app.
Uploading a count for a product that already has a result on that FSC-label overwrites that result.

Rows must either have a ProductID, ProductBackendID or ProductBarcode.
When any row is invalid, no results are processed and the invalid rows are returned in `Errors`.

EVA.Core.GiftCards.AddDigitalGiftCardToO.description:
A specific implementation for `AddProductToOrder` for GiftCards. Adds a new order line for a digital GiftCard to specified order, where
`OrderID` identifies the order for the customer and `Amount` is the desired amount to create a GiftCard for.

Optionally supply a `DetailsUrl` pointing to the website you want the buyer of the GiftCard to land to see/manage the order.

Additionally, the `DisplayOptions` property need to be supplied, this contains a bunch of default options to personalize the giftcard.
It is also possible to provide some Metadata. We won't do any processing on DisplayOptions.

Except: DetailsUrl will be changed to include the `OrderID` in the URL as well as a `token` that can be used to access a few services.

the order to be shipped (automatically when it is fully paid).

Additionally, this service can be called with an `AccessToken` and `GiftCardID` combination. In this case, no user validation is done - you know both
keys to the GiftCard, so you are allowed to get it's information.

If you want, you can specify a `LanguageID` to use for rendering the report - when omitted, the `LanguageID` of the current user.

See `GetDigitalGiftCardsForOrder` service for more details.

EVA.Core.GiftCards.GetDigitalGiftCardsFo.description:
Retrieve the GiftCard data for a specific order, based on given `OrderID`. This order needs to be visible for the current user.

Will return a list of `GiftCard` data, for every orderline with a GiftCard. Will return the same data supplied in the `AddGiftCardToOrder`
service. When the order was shipped (automatically when it is fully paid), the details `GiftCardNumber` and
`Pin` are also included. An additional property `IsAvailable` let's you check if it was indeed shipped and paid.

The `GiftCardID` returned on the GiftCard is it's unique identifier, to be used in conjunction with the `AccessToken` to make it globally
unique. Using the `AccessToken` and `GiftCardID`, we are pretty sure you are allowed to see the GiftCard data. Use this data to build the link
to share directly, or use the approperiate services to mail/text/print this.

Additionally, this service can be called with an `AccessToken` and `GiftCardID` combination, as explained above. In this case, no user validation
is done - you know both keys to the GiftCard, so you are allowed to get it's information.

EVA.Core.Management.FIFO.ListProductCost.description:
This service lets you view the ProductCostPriceLedger, optionally filtered by ProductID/OrganizationUnitID and others.

The ProductCostPriceLedger is used to determine the cost prices of stock for OrganizationUnits that use CostPriceCalculationMethod = Fifo.

For those OrganizationUnits, whenever stock is received in them, a record is stored in the ProductCostPriceLedger noting the quantity and the purchase price of that stock and then whenever
stock is reduced this ledger is consulted in a first-in-first-out manner to determine the cost price of that stock mutation. This service gives you insight into that ledger.

EVA.Core.Management.PaymentMethods.Migra.description:
Check or perform the migration for setting `PaymentMethods:PaymentTypeAvailabilityByOuSetType`.

Omitting `SaveChanges` will default to `false`, returning the changes it would have done, but don't actually persist them. Pass `true` explicitly if you want to actually migrate (use with caution!).

The payment type property `OrganizationUnitSetID` is hence-forth known as 'the legacy filter', where as the configured list of `OrganizationUnitSetPaymentType` is called 'the sets' or 'a set'.

Will execute for each active payment type;

- If it has no legacy filter configured, will remove any set that might be configured for this payment type
- If it *has* a legacy filter configured;
 - This legacy filter will be removed
 - If there is no matching set configured, it will add it
 - If there is a matching set configured but it is limited (disabled for delivery etc.), those limitations will be lifted
 - If there are any other set configured, those will be removed

And finally, the setting will be enabled on root level.

This migration will not run if the setting is already set (at any level!).

EVA.Core.Management.Stock.CreateStockAll.description:
Creates a StockAllocationRule for the SupplierOrganizationUnitID and OrganizationUnitID.

- If `ProductID` is left null, this is a 'catch-all' rule, meaning that the rule applies to all products (but it can still be overriden by a rule with a specific `ProductID`).
Only a reservation can be a catch-all rule, a limitation must specify a `ProductID` or a `ProductSearchTemplateID`.
- `RefillPeriodInDays` is deprecated. The refill schedule now lives on the supplier relation as a `SchedulingConfig`. When set on a `Limitation`, it is applied to that relation's schedule; it is ignored for a `Reservation`, as only a `Limitation` can be refilled.
- If `ValueType` is `Percentage`, then `Value` must be between 0 and 100.
- `OrganizationUnitSupplierID` is a reference to a supplier relationship between OrganizationUnits, not to an OrganizationUnit.
This is for example the supplier relationship between a warehouse and a store. Available OrganizationUnitSuppliers can be found through `ListOrganizationUnitSuppliers`.
- When left empty, OrganizationUnitID defaults to the OrganizationUnitID on the OrganizationUnitSupplier. So if the supplier relationship is between a warehouse and a store, this will
default to the store. When specified, the OrganizationUnitID *must* be one that the supplier of the relationship *directly* supplies to.
For example, if a supplier relationship exists between a warehouse and a country OrganizationUnit then you *can't* specify a store that falls
under that country OrganizationUnit. In that case, you should create a StockAllocationRule between the country and the store,
not between the warehouse and the store.

Priority.description: In case there is not enough stock, Priority is used to determine who gets preference. A higher Priority means a higher preference.

deprecated.comment: RefillPeriodInDays is deprecated and is scheduled to be removed in 2.0.886: The refill schedule moved to the supplier relation. When set on a Limitation, it is translated into that relation's SchedulingConfig (1 = daily, N = every N days). Set SchedulingConfig on the OrganizationUnitSupplier instead..

EVA.Core.Orders.AddProductToOrder.description:
Add a Product to an Order

A product can be defined by `ProductID` or `Barcode`.
If the product is unstackable (e.g. gift cards, same product added with different serial numbers), new orderlines are created.

Description.description: Optionally override the default description that is generated for the new OrderLine. If specified, this OrderLine will not be stacked on any existing OrderLines in the Order of the same Product (unless they use the same Description). Instead, a new OrderLine will be created.

ForceNewLine.description: This will always create a new line, regardless of whether a line with the same product ID was found in the order.

ParentID.description: Specify this field to add the new line as a child of the specified parent

UnitPriceInTax.description: If the product allows its price to be modified, you can specify the desired price using this field.

Description.description: Optionally override the default description that is generated for the new OrderLine.

EVA.Core.Orders.AddServiceProductToOrder.description: Adds a service product to an order.

EVA.Core.Orders.ApplySalesTaxEstimateFor.description: Will apply and return the estimated tax for specified order. Its effect is persistent through all subsequent calls for this orders' amounts.

EVA.Core.Orders.AttachConsumerCompanyToO.description: Attaches a consumer company to an order. Optionally, provide a user ID to associate with it.

EVA.Core.Orders.AttachCustomerToOrder.description: Attach a Customer to an Order. When no UserID is provided the current user will be attached. If the selected User has addresses, these will also be assigned to the Order.

AttachmentMetadata.description: Attachment Metadata to be added in the Order Ledger's Description.

EVA.Core.Orders.AttachIdentificationToOr.description: Attach an identification document to an order. This will replace any existing identification document attached to the order.

EVA.Core.Orders.AutocompleteOrder.description:
Attempts to autocomplete the order by:

- Cancelling the lines that can still be cancelled
- Invoicing the lines that've been (partially) shipped
- Optionally creating a payment to bring the open amount to 0

:bikini: __The actions this service performs are irreverisble__

*With great power comes great responsibility*
-Uncle Ben

GenerateFinancialEvents.description: When enabled, a payment financial event is generated for the balancing payment that brings the order's open amount to zero, in the current financial period. Defaults to false, keeping that booking to be handled manually.

IsUsable.description: False when this payment type cannot be used yet on this order. See NotUsableError for the reason.

MaximumAmount.description: When this field is set, the amount that can be paid with this method is limited.

NotUsableError.description: Populated when IsUsable is false. Type is a stable reason code; Message is human-readable.

Amount.description: Price of a single unit, before discounts, based on the SoldFromOrganizationUnit settings this should be in or ex tax. See service documentation.

BackendID.description: ID of the order line from the 3rd party

CustomID.description: Article number of the product from the 3rd party

GiftcardData.description: Used for passing in the data for a digital giftcard.

GiftcardMedia.description: Used for passing in the media information for a digital giftcard.

IsFinalSale.description: Marks the line as a final sale line, making it non returnable.

OriginalAmount.description: Original price of a single unit, before discounts, based on the SoldFromOrganizationUnit settings this should be in or ex tax. See service documentation.

PaymentLineIdentifier.description: Used for passing the identifier used to identify this line at the payment provider. This is required for payments that need capture on line level like Klarna.

PreferredFulfillmentOrganizationUnitBack.description:
Allows you to specify a preferred organization for doing the physical fulfillment of the OrderLine.
Depending on your order orchestration configuration this can be a hard filter or merely a preference.

SerialNumber.description: Used for passing in the serial number of, for example, a gift card. This is used to support refunding and other operations on the gift card.

TaxAmount.description: When known the exact TaxAmount can be specified. Used when tax calculations are done by an external party like Avatax.

TaxExemptionCode.description: A code identifying the tax exemption.

TaxExemptionReason.description: A longer description with the justification for the tax exemption.

TaxRate.description: When no tax rate is provided, the taxrate will be based on what is known in Eva. When no rate can be determined, an error will be thrown.

EVA.Core.Orders.CancelDiscountOrderLine.description:
Cancel a discount order line.

When the discount of the given line is a coupon triggerd discount, the coupon will be removed from the order.
When the discount of the given line is a manual discount, the manual discount will be cancelled.
When the discount of the given line is an automatic discount, the discount will be disabled on the order. To re-enable it you must call the 'EnableDisabledDiscountOnOrder' service. You can check which discount are disabled on an order by calling 'ListDisabledDiscountsOnOrder'

EVA.Core.Orders.CancelOrder.description:
Cancel a complete order or a subset of lines.

The order can be identified by an OrderID or by BackendID + BackendSystemID, the lines can be identified by an OrderLineID or by BackendID.

The result will tell you if it was successful.

AutoRefund.description: Try to refund the order if any cancellation was successful.

BackendID.description: Reference to the order that is being cancelled - required when `OrderID` is omitted

BackendSystemID.description: Reference to the system from which the order originated - required when `OrderID` is omitted

Force.description:
Forcing cancellations is not recommended! Requires `ForceCancelOrder` functionality.

      Only use this when a normal cancellation does not work, because the exported party (warehouse) does not accept it, and they have agreed that
      they too will manually cancel it in their systems. This will skip all external validation and cause discrepancies in this order status and stock levels.

OrderID.description: ID of the order that is being cancelled - required when `BackendID` and `BackendSystemID` are omitted

OrderLines.description: Lines to cancel - or, if none are specified, all open lines of the order will be cancelled

BackendID.description: Reference to the orderline that is being cancelled - required when `OrderLineID` is omitted

OrderLineID.description: ID of the orderline that is being cancelled - required when `BackendID` is omitted

Quantity.description: Quantity to be cancelled. If left blank the full order line will be cancelled

Reason.description: Reason for cancelling this line, stored on the order line and used as the stock mutation reason. Specific deployments may act on it, for example setting warehouse stock to zero when the item is out of stock.

EVA.Core.Orders.ChangeOrderLinesToCarryO.description:
Update some OrderLines to a state so that they can be carried out in a store

If the products should be ordered from a supplier first, the `OrderTheLinesFromASupplier` property should be true.

When no OrderLineIDs are provided all eligable lines in the Order are updated

MustBeOrdered.description: Set to true to indicate that you don't have stock available for carry-out and that you want to order the products from a supplier when the order is placed.

EVA.Core.Orders.ChangeOrderLinesToDelive.description:
Update some OrderLines to a state so that they can be delivered to the ShippingAddress on the order

When no OrderLineIDs are provided all eligable lines in the Order are updated

EVA.Core.Orders.ChangeOrderLinesToPickup.description:
Update some OrderLines to a state so that they can be pickup up in a store by the customer attached to the order

If no PickupOrganizationUnit was chosen yet, it should be provided in the `PickupOrganizationUnitID` property.

When no OrderLineIDs are provided all eligable lines in the Order are updated

PickupOrganizationUnitID.description: Will keep the current value when not provided.

EVA.Core.Orders.CheckOrderAddressFraud.description: Check if the order has fraudulent shipping or billing addresses

EVA.Core.Orders.CreateInvoicedOrderLineC.description:
Create a correction on an already invoiced line.

This can be used to refund a partial amount on a completed OrderLine, in cases where the product should still be returnable.

Specify either `OrderLineID` and `CorrectionAmount`, or `Lines`.

- If the product is not returnable anymore, a return without retake should be created
- This will result in a new line that will be invoiced immediately and shipped by default (AutoProcess.Ship is the default variant).
- If the shipping isn't desired, use AutoProcess.None;
- If a refund is desired, use AutoProcess.ShipAndRefund.

IncludingTax.description: Specify whether the amount includes tax. When true, amounts are considered tax-inclusive. When not specified, corrections are made based on order's tax handling mode.

EVA.Core.Orders.CreateOfferFromOrder.description: Converts an order to an offer

Create a new order.

The order will be created in the organization unit specified by `OrganizationUnitID`, or in the current organization unit of the client if not provided.

- For employee- and API users, requires `Order:Create` functionality in the specified organization unit
- For anonymous- and customer users, the specified organization unit must be your current organization unit, and it must allow ecommerce access

Documents.description:
List of order document outputs available for a specific order.
Each document contains information regarding the following categories:

`Receipt`           - physically printing the order invoice
`Paper`             - printing the order invoice on a paper printer
`Email`             - sending the order invoice by email
`Digital`           - providing a downloadable version of the order invoice
`ElectronicReceipt` - providing an electronic receipt version of the order invoice
`Metadata`          - providing information about the order invoice.

The document category contains information on whether it's available for the order
and a reason code in case it's not available.

Allowed.description: Allowed is false when this option cannot be used, true otherwise

Preferred.description: Indicates if this output should be preferred by the frontend. Can be used to, for example, set a checkbox or radio button by default so the user does not have to toggle it themselves

ReasonCode.description: Optional reason code that is included if Allowed is set to false

Stations.description: Possbile stations where the document can be output

ID.description: ID of the Station in EVA. Can be used directly in services

Name.description: Name of the station for display purposes

It is required to supply an `OrderID` or a `ShipmentID`.

When using an `OrderID` it is also required to set the `LinesToShip`.

When a `StationID` is supplied the documents will be printed, if not, the service will return urls for downloading the documents.

OrderID.description: Required when omitting `ShipmentID`.

OriginalCreationDate.description: Original date when this order was created

OriginalInvoiceDate.description: Original date when this order was invoiced

CreatedByFullName.description: Only populated in case the CreatedBy user in an employee

HasExplicitCompany.description: Indicates whether the company was explicitly attached to the order.

IsTradeIn.description: Indicates if the order is a trade-in (the order has a return line with a product of type `SecondChance`).

LocalInformation.description: Information related to local mode, in case it was imported from LiveGuard.

Repair.description: The repair this order is associated with.

IsQualifier.description: True when this line qualified (triggered) the promotion rather than receiving the benefit, e.g. the purchased line in buy-one-get-one. Qualifier lines carry no discount amount.

DisplayProperties.description: Properties that should be used for display in the frontends to keep a matching experience in all apps.

QuantityOrdered.description: This is the quantity that was ordered. Make sure you really need this property, the total of the line is TotalQuantityToShip.

WasOrdered.description: Indicates that this orderline was originally a backorder (order from supplier) before the LineActionType potentially changed.

WasReserved.description: Indicates that this orderline was originally a reservation (pickup from store) before the LineActionType potentially changed.

EVA.Core.Orders.DuplicateOrder.description:

* To include the orignal GiftWrapping the flag `IncludeGiftWrapping` should be set to true. When combining this with a subset of lines, this can generate an error when some wrapped lines are not duplicated.
* To ignore shipping costs, set `IgnoreShippingCosts` to true (defaults to false)

EVA.Core.Orders.ExemptOrderFromTax.description:
Marks the provided Order or OrderLine as exempt from tax, with specified code and reason.

When exempting the Order, this also marks all current OrderLines of the Order that haven't been invoiced yet as tax-exempt. All future
OrderLines created on this Order will then also automatically be made tax-exempt.

Calling this service is irreversible; once the Order is marked as tax exempt, it cannot be undone and can only be worked around by creating a new Order.

TaxExemptionCode.description: A code identifying the tax exemption.

TaxExemptionReason.description: A longer description with the justification for the tax exemption.

TaxExemptionVerification.description: This verification number is a confirmation of the tax exemption reason.

EVA.Core.Orders.GetOrder.description:
Get an Order by ID.

This service is readonly, it will not update the order just by calling it like the `GetShoppingCart` service does.

To include the result of `GetRequiredDataForOrder`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.RequiredFor` can be set to the desired level of requirements.
To include the result of `GetProductRequirementValuesForOrder`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludeProductRequirements` can be set to `true`.
To include the result of `GetGiftWrappingOptionsForOrder` and `GetAvailableGiftWrappingLinesForOrder`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludeGiftWrapping` can be set to `true`.
To include the result of `PrefigureDiscounts` and `GetPotentialDiscountsForOrder`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludePrefigureDiscounts` can be set to `true`.
To include the result of `GetPickProductDiscountOptionsForOrder`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludePickProductOptions` can be set to `true`.
To include the result of `ListAvailableShippingMethods`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludeAvailableShippingMethods` can be set to `true`.
To include the result of `GetAvailablePaymentMethods`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludeAvailablePaymentMethods` can be set to `true`.
To include the result of `GetAvailableRefundPaymentMethodsForOrder`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludeAvailableRefundPaymentMethods` can be set to `true`.
To include the result of `ValidateOrderShipment`, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludeValidateShipment` can be set to `true`.
To include the available actions for the PaymentTransactions, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.IncludePaymentTransactionActions` can be set to `true`.

EVA.Core.Orders.GetReturnableStatusForOr.description:
Gets whether or not an Order is currently returnable.

For each OrderLine on the Order you'll get back a result that specifies whether or not it can be returned,
how much can be returned and which (if any) other OrderLines must be returned before the line itself can be returned
(think of parent-child lines where you can't return a child OrderLine without also returning the parent OrderLine).

In addition, this service may return `ReturnSets` which specify that 'if you return these OrderLines (specified by `OrderLineIDs`) then
you must *also* return these lines (specified by `RequiredOrderLineIDsToReturn`). For example, if you return all normal OrderLines on an Order
then you must also return all the free products you have received.

Finally, specify the `ReturningQuantities` parameter as an object where the key is an `OrderLineID` with a (positive) `Quantity` you wish to be
returned. The `Result` can be affected in case rules have been configured to, for example, allow _returns without products_ only when the total
return order amount is below a certain amount.

RequiresSpecialInStoreReturn.description: Indicates whether the order needs to use the special return procedure for in-store returns. This is done using the `CreateInStoreReturn` service.

EVA.Core.Orders.GetReturnableStatusForPr.description: Gets whether or not a product is returnable for an unreferenced return. Evaluates the ReturnableStatus script and product-level non-returnable checks (product type, gift card configuration).

EVA.Core.Orders.GiftWrapping.SetGiftWrap.description:
Set the GiftWrapping options on an Order.

There are 4 options:

 - Wrap the complete order: set `WrapOrder` to `true`
 - Wrap the complete order individually: set `WrapIndividually` to `true`
 - Wrap parts of the order: set `GiftWraps` with a set of wraps
 - Wrap nothing: set everything to `null`

A `GiftWrap` consists out of an optional `Message` (could be printed on a card), an optional `GreetingCardProductID` and a set of `WrapLines`. A
`WrapLine` has an `OrderLineID` and a `Quantity`.

If a `GreetingCardProductID` and/or `Message` is desired when the order should be completely wrapped, or without any giftwrapping at all, set these
properties on root level. In all other cases they should be set on the `GiftWraps`.

EVA.Core.Orders.PushReturnOrder.description:
Creates a returnorder with all specified data

It is required to send the identifier for the ReturnOrder of the external system by providing a BackendSystemID and a BackendID.

A return is based of an OriginalOrder. This order can be identifier by the OriginalBackendID or the OriginalOrderID. One of those is required.

If the stock is already received, set the `AlreadyReceived` to true. This will ship the order immediately.

If the stock is already received and the open amount should be refunded directly, set `AutoRefund` to true.

The Lines have to be identified by the original line, this should be done by providing the OriginalBackendID or the OriginalOrderLineID.
If those are not available the CustomID of the product can be set, but matching based on that is not advised.

Return is booked in the logged-in OU, unless otherwise specified by `ReturnToOrganizationUnitBackendID` or `ReturnToOriginalOrganizationUnit`.

AutoRefund.description: Try to refund the order immediately. The remaining open-for-refund amount is computed after any externally-recorded `Payments` are applied.

BackendID.description: A unique identifier for the order, within the context of given `BackendSystemID`

BackendSystemID.description: A code, free of choice for the calling 3rd party application creating the order

CustomerID.description: Specify the customer for an unreferenced return.

IsCustomerReturn.description: If this order pending a customer return

IsOffer.description: Specifies if the order is an offer - this is only happening if AutoRefund or AlreadyReceived are set to false. If no value is specified, the default is false.

OriginalBackendID.description: The unique identifier of the original order, within the context of given `BackendSystemID`

Payments.description: Optional payments to record against the return order. Each entry mirrors `PushSalesOrder.Payments`; a negative `Amount` represents a refund already paid out externally (e.g. via the PSP).

ReturnToOrganizationUnitBackendID.description: Where the return will be booked.

ReturnToOriginalOrganizationUnit.description: When true, book the return against the original order's organization unit. Ignored for unreferenced returns and when `ReturnToOrganizationUnitBackendID` is set.

SendInvoice.description: Sends an invoice (credit note) - this is only done if AutoRefund or AlreadyReceived are also true, and requires a customer to be set

Amount.description: Price of a single unit, before discounts, based on the SoldFromOrganizationUnit settings this should be in or ex tax. See service documentation. This amount applies to unreferenced returns only.

CustomID.description: Article number of the product from the 3rd party

OriginalBackendID.description: ID of the original orderline from the 3rd party

Quantity.description: Quantity that has been returned, positive

ReturnStockLabel.description: Return stock label for the returned goods. When omitted, the label is resolved from configuration, for referenced returns defaulting to the original line's label when that is returnable. For referenced returns the label must be configured as a returnable stock label for the organization unit receiving the stock (`StockOrganizationUnitID` when provided, otherwise the organization unit the return is booked in); a label that is not returnable there results in an error. For unreferenced returns a non-returnable label silently falls back to the default returnable label.

IgnoreDiscounts.description: Add `IgnoreDiscounts` option on the order. Defaults to true.

IgnoreGiftWrappingCosts.description: Add `IgnoreGiftWrappingCosts` option on the order. Defaults to true

IgnoreShippingCosts.description: Add `IgnoreShippingCosts` option on the order. Defaults to true

Amount.description: Amount of the payment that was actually paid. For a refund (return paid out to customer) supply a negative value, mirroring the rest of EVA.

AutoConfirm.description:
Whether to automatically confirm the payment or adhere to the payment type configuration.
The default value is set to true.

BackendID.description: Identifier of the payment by the 3rd party (e.g. the one from the payment service provider (PSP))

Part (or all) of the amount that has already been captured for this payment.
This amount should always be in the base currency of the order.

If this is set to not None, the Payment will not be considered captured, but only Authorized. This means the capture will be done based on this value.
If it's not set, the CaptureMoment will be determined based on the PaymentType.

It indicates the specific amount paid in the foreign currency.

ForeignCurrencyID.description:

It indicates the currency used for the payment.

When no Suppliers are available, no Order can be generated.

EVA.Core.Orders.SearchOrders.description:
Search for any type of orders by providing the filter details properties
Important search criterias are: OrganizationUnitID, CurrentOrganizationUnitType, OrderIDs, CustomerID(ClientContext.Type), PaymentStatus.

When no StartTime is provided this will be defaulted to 3 months ago. The only exception is when specific OrderIDs are provided, then it's allowed to not specify a Date.

To include the custom fields of the customer, the property `AdditionalOrderDataOptions.CustomerCustomFields` can be set to `true`.

E.g. request:
{
  "OrderIDs": [
    "orderID1",
    "orderID2"
  ],
  "PaymentStatus": "PaymentStatus",
  "IsShipped": "isShipped"
}


Payment status options:
    NotPaid = 0,
    Paid = 1,
    Partial = 2

EVA.Core.Orders.SetOrderBackendIdentifie.description:
Sets `BackendID`/`BackendSystemID` on specified `OrderID`.

This combination may not already exist, and the targeted order may not be completed, or  already have a `BackendID`/`BackendSystemID` set.

:warning: Careful! Use at your own risk!

An order may already have any of the following things, which will not automatically be regenerated/resent because of this identifier change, and could
result in mapping issues on any external system listening in on these. Any of these would also apply to return orders referencing this order, or stock
mutations that have been caused by this order.

* Order exports to third parties
* Event exports (order created, order updated, ...)
* Data Lake exports
* Shipment labels with third party carriers
* Financial exports (Cookbook)
* Created documents (receipts, invoices, ...)

- The user must have type `Employee`
- This service can only be called on orders that have not been invoiced yet
- As `SoldBy` is a line-level property this service will update all lines on the order that have not been invoiced yet

If specified, sets the `SoldBy` only for the given order lines.

:notebook: Newly created order lines will not automatically inherit `SoldBy` set on invidivual order lines

EVA.Core.Pricing.CreateTaxRate.description:
Creates a tax rate.

* `CountryID` is a foreign key to the Countries table, which uses the ISO 3166-2 standard as ID
* `CountrySubdivisionID` is a foreign key to the CountrySubdivisions table, which uses the ISO 3166-2 standard as ID
* `TaxCodeID` is a foreign key to the TaxCodes table, which can be listed using the `ListTaxCodes` service

Percentages are a human readable formatted result of a fraction - applications use a `Rate` instead as an actual result of fraction to maintain
precision and integrity. If you wish to set a 21% tax percentage, that means a 1.21 tax rate. Setting a rate of 1.00 implies a 0% tax percentage,
and setting to 2.00 would mean a rediculous 100% tax percentage, doubling prices. You can probably tell that a `Rate` of 2.00 here is much more
readable than a 100% increase, but hey; nobody's forcing you to stick to percentages. At least - we're not!

Oh, and you can set a tax rate of 0.00, which would mean it will be fully sponsored by the government and will be free to purchase. The services
block anything lower than 0.00 and higher than 2.00 for sanity reasons. Will recap when governments gone mad.

:key: The combination of `CountryID`, `CountrySubdivision` and `TaxCodeID` is unique and will be enforced by EVA.

:point_right: `StartDate` and `EndDate` are optional, and can be used to transition from one rate to a next when it changes. Both these dates
are inclusive, meaning you'd want to set the `EndDate` of the expiring tax rate to 2018-12-31 and the `StartDate` of the new tax rate to
2019-01-01 (for example).

Category.description:
Defines in which category the provided Rate falls for the provided CountryID. For example, a rate of 25% in the country Denmark should have Category = High as 25% is the high VAT rate in Denmark.

If the TaxCode used for this TaxRate is one of the predefined ones (High, Low, Zero, Exempt, Intermediate) this parameter is ignored but Category must be provided when using a custom TaxCode.

The Category `Dynamic` should be used for countries such as the US where the actual tax rate is context dependent and calculated dynamically.
